views.name: department_degree_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT d.department_id, d.department_name, COUNT(dp.degree_program_id) AS degree_count FROM Departments d LEFT JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON dp.department_id = d.department_id GROUP BY d.department_id, d.department_name
views.description: Per-department counts of degree program records (one row per department with department id, name, and degree count) to support analyses of degree distribution across departments.
validated_on: What is the name and id of the department with the most number of degrees ?
How many departments offer any degree?
How many different departments offer degrees?

provenance.question: Which department offers the most number of degrees? List department name and id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the department (name and id) that offers the largest number of degrees, returning the department's name and id for the department(s) with the maximum count of degrees offered.
Required outputs: department name; department id
Filters: Count degrees per department across all degree records; include only department(s) whose degree count equals the maximum degree count observed (i.e., return ties if multiple departments share the highest number). No other row-level filters.; Treat every degree record as contributing one to its department's degree total (no additional exclusions).
Sort/limit: no particular ordering required; return all department rows that tie for the maximum count (no numeric limit)

tests.purpose: View has one row per department (no duplicate department_id, department_name pairs)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT department_id, department_name, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM department_degree_counts GROUP BY department_id, department_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: degree_count equals count of Degree_Programs linked to the department (reconciliation with base table)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM department_degree_counts v LEFT JOIN Departments d ON v.department_id = d.department_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) AS actual_count FROM Degree_Programs GROUP BY department_id) dp ON d.department_id = dp.department_id WHERE COALESCE(v.degree_count,0) != COALESCE(dp.actual_count,0)

tests.purpose: No NULLs in the key columns department_id or department_name
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM department_degree_counts WHERE department_id IS NULL OR department_name IS NULL

positive_subgoals:
Task: Find the department that has the largest number of degrees and return that department's name and id.
Required outputs: department name; department id
Filters: Consider departments that have one or more associated degree records.; If multiple departments tie for the largest number of degrees, return all tied departments.
Sort/limit: order by descending degree count; no fixed numeric limit (return all ties for top count)

Task: Compute the number of departments that offer any degree (i.e., count distinct departments that offer at least one degree).
Required outputs: count of departments that offer any degree
Filters: Include only departments that have at least one associated degree record (i.e., departments with one or more degrees). Do not count departments with zero degrees.

Task: Compute the number of distinct departments that offer degrees.
Required outputs: count_of_distinct_departments: an integer representing how many different departments offer at least one degree
Filters: Consider only rows where a department is recorded as 'offering a degree' (i.e., associated with at least one degree record).; Treat departments with the same name as identical (count unique department identifiers or names).; Exclude null or missing department identifiers/names from the count.

views.name: course_section_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT c.course_id, c.course_name, COUNT(s.section_id) AS section_count FROM Courses c LEFT JOIN Sections s ON s.course_id = c.course_id GROUP BY c.course_id, c.course_name
views.description: Per-course counts of linked sections (number of sections per course), including course id and name for joining
counter_examples: What are the names and ids of every course with less than 2 sections?

provenance.question: What are the names and id of courses having at most 2 sections?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Return the course names and course ids for every course that has at most 2 sections.
Required outputs: course name; course id
Filters: Include only rows for courses whose number of sections is less than or equal to 2; Count sections per course using whatever table/column represents sections linked to a course (i.e., group by course id)

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows per grain (course_id, course_name) in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT course_id, course_name, COUNT(*) AS dup_count FROM course_section_counts GROUP BY course_id, course_name HAVING dup_count > 1)

tests.purpose: section_count matches count of Sections linked to each course (recomputed from base tables)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM course_section_counts v LEFT JOIN Courses c ON v.course_id = c.course_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT course_id, COUNT(section_id) AS real_count FROM Sections GROUP BY course_id) s ON v.course_id = s.course_id WHERE COALESCE(s.real_count, 0) != v.section_count

tests.purpose: Keys (course_id and course_name) are not NULL in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM course_section_counts WHERE course_id IS NULL OR course_name IS NULL

negative_subgoals:
Task: Return the name and id of every course that has fewer than 2 sections.
Required outputs: course name; course id
Filters: count of sections associated with the course < 2

views.name: semester_registration_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT s.semester_id, s.semester_name, COUNT(se.student_enrolment_id) AS registration_count FROM Semesters s JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON se.semester_id = s.semester_id GROUP BY s.semester_id, s.semester_name
views.description: Per-semester counts of student registrations (one row per semester with semester_id, semester_name, and registration_count) for use in further aggregation or ranking.

provenance.question: What is the semester which most student registered in? Show both the name and the id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the semester (both its name and its id) that has the largest number of student registrations.
Required outputs: semester id; semester name
Filters: Count registrations per semester across all students; include only semester(s) with the maximum registration count (if tie, return all tied semesters).
Sort/limit: order by registration count descending, limit to the top count (no numeric limit if ties should be returned)

tests.purpose: View has exactly one row per semester (no duplicate rows with same semester_id and semester_name)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT semester_id, semester_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM semester_registration_counts GROUP BY semester_id, semester_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: registration_count matches the count of Student_Enrolment rows per semester from base tables
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semester_registration_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT semester_id, COUNT(student_enrolment_id) AS expected_count FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY semester_id) b ON v.semester_id = b.semester_id WHERE COALESCE(v.registration_count, -9223372036854775808) != COALESCE(b.expected_count, -9223372036854775808)

tests.purpose: No NULL keys: semester_id and semester_name must not be NULL
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semester_registration_counts WHERE semester_id IS NULL OR semester_name IS NULL

views.name: semester_student_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT se.semester_id, COUNT(se.student_id) AS student_count FROM Student_Enrolment se GROUP BY se.semester_id
views.description: Per-semester counts of students enrolled (one row per semester with semester id and student count) useful for ranking or join with semester metadata.

provenance.question: For each semester, what is the name and id of the one with the most students registered?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: For each semester, identify the single record (semester) participant entry that has the largest number of students registered and return that semester's name and id.
Required outputs: semester name; semester id
Filters: Consider only rows grouped by semester (i.e., compute the count of students registered per semester).; For each semester, select the row corresponding to the maximum number of students registered for that semester.; If there are ties for the maximum number of students within a semester, include exactly one arbitrary tied semester entry (deterministic tie-breaking can be applied if available, otherwise pick one).
Sort/limit: Return one output row per semester; no global ordering required.

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows per grain: each semester_id appears at most once in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT semester_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM semester_student_counts GROUP BY semester_id HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: student_count equals count of distinct student_id rows in base table per semester (detects incorrect aggregation or missing GROUP BY on source)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semester_student_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT semester_id, COUNT(se.student_id) AS expected_count FROM Student_Enrolment se GROUP BY se.semester_id) b ON v.semester_id = b.semester_id WHERE (b.expected_count IS NULL AND v.student_count IS NOT NULL) OR (b.expected_count IS NOT NULL AND v.student_count != b.expected_count)

tests.purpose: Every row's semester_id in the view must exist in the base table (no phantom semesters produced)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semester_student_counts v WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Student_Enrolment se WHERE se.semester_id = v.semester_id)

views.name: student_semester_degree_program_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT student_id, semester_id, COUNT(DISTINCT degree_program_id) AS degree_program_count
FROM Student_Enrolment
GROUP BY student_id, semester_id
views.description: For each student and semester, count of distinct degree programs the student is enrolled in (one row per student_id and semester_id with the program count).
counter_examples: What are the first, middle, and last names, along with the ids, of all students who enrolled in 2 degree programs in one semester?

provenance.question: Who are enrolled in 2 degree programs in one semester? List the first name, middle name and last name and the id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find all students who are enrolled in exactly two degree programs during the same single semester; return each matching student's first name, middle name, last name, and id.
Required outputs: first name; middle name; last name; id
Filters: student must have two distinct degree program enrollments that occur in the same semester (same semester identifier); count of distinct degree programs for that student in that semester = 2; exclude students with fewer or more than 2 degree programs in that semester

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (student_id, semester_id) in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_semester_degree_program_counts v JOIN (SELECT student_id, semester_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM student_semester_degree_program_counts GROUP BY student_id, semester_id HAVING cnt > 1) d ON v.student_id = d.student_id AND v.semester_id = d.semester_id

tests.purpose: degree_program_count equals the distinct count of degree_program_id in base table for that student and semester
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_semester_degree_program_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT student_id, semester_id, COUNT(DISTINCT degree_program_id) AS expected_cnt FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY student_id, semester_id) b ON v.student_id = b.student_id AND v.semester_id = b.semester_id WHERE (b.expected_cnt IS NULL AND v.degree_program_count IS NOT NULL) OR (b.expected_cnt IS NOT NULL AND v.degree_program_count <> b.expected_cnt)

tests.purpose: Keys student_id and semester_id are not NULL in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_semester_degree_program_counts WHERE student_id IS NULL OR semester_id IS NULL

negative_subgoals:
Task: Find all students who enrolled in exactly 2 degree programs within the same semester, and return each such student's first name, middle name, last name, and student id.
Required outputs: first name; middle name; last name; id (student id)
Filters: Count of distinct degree program enrollments for the student within a single semester must be exactly 2; Enrollments considered must share the same semester identifier (e.g., same term/session and year) for each counted pair; Include only students for whom such a semester exists

views.name: students_enrolled_in_degree_program
views.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT s.student_id, s.first_name, s.middle_name, s.last_name, se.degree_program_id, dp.degree_summary_name
FROM Student_Enrolment se
JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON se.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id
JOIN Students s ON se.student_id = s.student_id
views.description: All students who have an enrollment linking them to a degree program, with student name parts and the associated degree program identifier and degree summary name for reuse/filtering by degree level.

provenance.question: Who is enrolled in a Bachelor degree program? List the first name, middle name, last name.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find all persons who are enrolled in a Bachelor degree program and return their name parts.
Required outputs: first name; middle name; last name
Filters: Enrollment records must indicate the person is currently enrolled in a program whose degree level is 'Bachelor' (or equivalent string 'Bachelors'/'B.Sc' if present) — include only rows where the program/degree level equals 'Bachelor'.; Include each person only if there exists an enrollment linking that person to such a Bachelor program.; Return all matching persons (no additional filtering by date, active flag, or program type unless those are required by the schema to define 'enrolled').

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (student_id, first_name, middle_name, last_name, degree_program_id, degree_summary_name).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT student_id, first_name, middle_name, last_name, degree_program_id, degree_summary_name, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM students_enrolled_in_degree_program GROUP BY student_id, first_name, middle_name, last_name, degree_program_id, degree_summary_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Every row in the view corresponds to an existing Student_Enrolment row (join didn't fabricate rows).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students_enrolled_in_degree_program v LEFT JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON v.student_id = se.student_id AND v.degree_program_id = se.degree_program_id WHERE se.student_enrolment_id IS NULL

tests.purpose: No nulls in key columns of the view (student_id and degree_program_id must be present).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students_enrolled_in_degree_program WHERE student_id IS NULL OR degree_program_id IS NULL

views.name: student_count_per_degree_program_kind
views.body_sql: SELECT dp.degree_summary_name AS program_kind, COUNT(DISTINCT se.student_id) AS student_count FROM Student_Enrolment se JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON se.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id WHERE se.degree_program_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY dp.degree_summary_name
views.description: Per program kind (degree_summary_name) count of distinct students enrolled in any degree program

provenance.question: Find the kind of program which most number of students are enrolled in?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Identify which program kind has the largest number of enrolled students and return that program kind along with the student count.
Required outputs: program kind (the kind/type/category of program); student count (number of students enrolled in that program kind)
Filters: consider all students and their enrollments across all program kinds; count each student enrollment toward the program kind they are enrolled in; include only program kinds that have at least one enrolled student
Sort/limit: order results by student count descending and return the top 1

tests.purpose: No NULLs in key column program_kind
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_count_per_degree_program_kind WHERE program_kind IS NULL

tests.purpose: student_count matches COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) computed from base tables per program_kind
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_count_per_degree_program_kind v LEFT JOIN (SELECT dp.degree_summary_name AS program_kind, COUNT(DISTINCT se.student_id) AS expected_count FROM Student_Enrolment se JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON se.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id WHERE se.degree_program_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY dp.degree_summary_name) b USING (program_kind) WHERE (v.student_count IS NULL AND b.expected_count IS NOT NULL) OR (v.student_count IS NOT NULL AND b.expected_count IS NULL) OR (v.student_count <> b.expected_count)

tests.purpose: Every row in view corresponds to at least one enrolment joined to a degree program (no spurious program_kind)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_count_per_degree_program_kind v LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT dp.degree_summary_name AS program_kind FROM Student_Enrolment se JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON se.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id WHERE se.degree_program_id IS NOT NULL) b USING (program_kind) WHERE b.program_kind IS NULL

views.name: degree_program_student_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT dp.degree_program_id, dp.degree_summary_name, COUNT(DISTINCT se.student_id) AS student_count FROM Degree_Programs dp JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON se.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id GROUP BY dp.degree_program_id, dp.degree_summary_name
views.description: Per degree program (including its degree_summary_name), the distinct count of enrolled students aggregated across all student_enrolment records.

provenance.question: What is the degree summary name that has the most number of students enrolled?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the degree summary name that has the largest number of enrolled students.
Required outputs: degree summary name (the name/label identifying a degree summary); student count for that degree summary (number of students enrolled)
Filters: consider all degree summaries present in the data; count students enrolled per degree summary across all records
Sort/limit: order by student count descending, limit 1

tests.purpose: View has one row per (degree_program_id, degree_summary_name) — detect duplicate rows in the view's grain
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT degree_program_id, degree_summary_name FROM degree_program_student_counts GROUP BY degree_program_id, degree_summary_name HAVING COUNT(*) > 1)

tests.purpose: student_count equals COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) computed from base table for each degree_program — detect mismatched aggregates
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM degree_program_student_counts v LEFT JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON v.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id WHERE (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT se.student_id) FROM Student_Enrolment se WHERE se.degree_program_id = v.degree_program_id) IS NOT v.student_count

tests.purpose: Every view row references an existing degree_program (no dangling foreign keys)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM degree_program_student_counts v LEFT JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON v.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id WHERE dp.degree_program_id IS NULL

views.name: program_student_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT dp.degree_program_id, dp.degree_summary_name, COUNT(se.student_enrolment_id) AS student_count FROM Degree_Programs dp LEFT JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON se.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id GROUP BY dp.degree_program_id, dp.degree_summary_name
views.description: Per-degree-program counts of enrolled students (one row per program with program id, program summary, and student enrollment count).

provenance.question: Find the program which most number of students are enrolled in. List both the id and the summary.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Return the program (its id and summary) that has the largest number of students enrolled.
Required outputs: program id; program summary
Filters: Consider all programs and count how many students are enrolled in each program using whatever enrollment relation exists between students and programs.; Select the program(s) with the maximum student count (if there is a tie, include all tied programs).
Sort/limit: order by student count desc; limit to the maximum count (no fixed numeric limit)

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (each degree_program_id + degree_summary_name appears at most once).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT degree_program_id, degree_summary_name, COUNT(*) AS c FROM program_student_counts GROUP BY degree_program_id, degree_summary_name HAVING c > 1)

tests.purpose: student_count matches COUNT of Student_Enrolment rows for that program (reconciles measure with base table), accounting for LEFT JOIN semantics (0 when no enrolments).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM program_student_counts p LEFT JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON p.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Student_Enrolment se WHERE se.degree_program_id = p.degree_program_id) != COALESCE(p.student_count, 0)

tests.purpose: Keys are not NULL: degree_program_id and degree_summary_name must be non-NULL for every row.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM program_student_counts WHERE degree_program_id IS NULL OR degree_summary_name IS NULL

views.name: degree_programs_with_enrolment_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT dp.degree_program_id, dp.degree_summary_name, dp.degree_summary_description, dp.department_id, dp.other_details, COALESCE(se.students_enrolled, 0) AS students_enrolled
FROM Degree_Programs dp
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT degree_program_id, COUNT(*) AS students_enrolled
  FROM Student_Enrolment
  GROUP BY degree_program_id
) se ON dp.degree_program_id = se.degree_program_id
views.description: Per-degree program counts of enrolled students by joining degree programs to student enrollment and aggregating enrollment count per degree program.

provenance.question: What is the program id and the summary of the degree that has the most students enrolled?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the degree record that has the largest number of students enrolled and return that degree's program id and its summary.
Required outputs: program id of the degree with the highest students enrolled; summary text of that same degree
Filters: consider only rows representing degrees; among those, choose the row(s) whose students enrolled value is maximal (i.e., equal to the greatest numeric students enrolled in the degrees table)
Sort/limit: order by students enrolled descending limit 1

tests.purpose: No duplicate degree_program_id in the view (view should be keyed by degree_program_id).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT degree_program_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM degree_programs_with_enrolment_counts GROUP BY degree_program_id HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: students_enrolled matches the count of Student_Enrolment rows per degree_program_id (including zero when none).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT dp.degree_program_id, dp.students_enrolled, COALESCE(se.cnt,0) AS expected FROM degree_programs_with_enrolment_counts dp LEFT JOIN (SELECT degree_program_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY degree_program_id) se ON dp.degree_program_id = se.degree_program_id WHERE dp.students_enrolled != COALESCE(se.cnt,0))

tests.purpose: Every degree_program_id in the view exists in the base Degree_Programs table (join did not introduce phantom keys).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM degree_programs_with_enrolment_counts v LEFT JOIN Degree_Programs dp USING (degree_program_id) WHERE dp.degree_program_id IS NULL

views.name: student_enrollment_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) AS enrollment_count FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY student_id
views.description: Per-student counts of enrollment records (number of enrollments per student), including student identifier for joining to student details.

provenance.question: Which student has enrolled for the most times in any program? List the id, first name, middle name, last name, the number of enrollments and student id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the student or students who have the highest count of enrollments across any program (i.e., the maximum number of times a student appears as enrolled), and return identifying name fields and counts for those student(s).
Required outputs: id; first name; middle name; last name; the number of enrollments; student id
Filters: Consider all enrollment records in the database; group enrollments by student and count the number of enrollments per student; select only the student(s) whose enrollment count equals the maximum count observed across all students.
Sort/limit: order results by student id ascending (or leave unspecified) and return all students tied for the maximum (no numeric limit)

tests.purpose: View has one row per student_id (no duplicate student_id keys)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM student_enrollment_counts GROUP BY student_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1)

tests.purpose: enrollment_count matches COUNT(*) of Student_Enrolment per student_id
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT v.student_id FROM student_enrollment_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) AS expected_count FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY student_id) b ON v.student_id = b.student_id WHERE (b.expected_count IS NULL AND v.enrollment_count != 0) OR (b.expected_count IS NOT NULL AND v.enrollment_count != b.expected_count))

tests.purpose: Every student_id in the view is NOT NULL and exists in base Student_Enrolment (no NULL keys, no phantom keys)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_enrollment_counts v WHERE v.student_id IS NULL OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Student_Enrolment s WHERE s.student_id = v.student_id)

views.name: student_enrollment_counts_13
views.body_sql: SELECT s.student_id, s.first_name, s.middle_name, s.last_name, COUNT(se.student_enrolment_id) AS enrollment_count FROM Students s JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON se.student_id = s.student_id GROUP BY s.student_id, s.first_name, s.middle_name, s.last_name
views.description: Per-student counts of enrollment records (number of enrollments) alongside student identifying fields for reuse in joins and ranking queries.

provenance.question: What is the first, middle, and last name, along with the id and number of enrollments, for the student who enrolled the most in any program?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the student who has the highest number of enrollments in any program and return that student's first name, middle name, last name, id, and the student's number of enrollments.
Required outputs: first name; middle name; last name; id; number of enrollments
Filters: Consider each student's total number of enrollments across programs (count of enrollment records linked to the student).; Select the student whose total number of enrollments is maximal (if multiple students tie for the maximum, return all such students).
Sort/limit: Order not required; limit to rows where the student's number of enrollments equals the maximum (no numeric limit unless tie handling causes multiple rows).

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (student_id, first_name, middle_name, last_name)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT student_id, first_name, middle_name, last_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM student_enrollment_counts_13 GROUP BY student_id, first_name, middle_name, last_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Each enrollment_count equals the number of Student_Enrolment rows for that student (measure reconciliation)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_enrollment_counts_13 v LEFT JOIN (SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) AS expected_count FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY student_id) b ON v.student_id = b.student_id WHERE (b.expected_count IS NULL AND v.enrollment_count != 0) OR (b.expected_count IS NOT NULL AND v.enrollment_count != b.expected_count)

tests.purpose: Keys used in the grain are not NULL
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_enrollment_counts_13 WHERE student_id IS NULL OR first_name IS NULL OR last_name IS NULL

views.name: semesters_with_no_enrolments
views.body_sql:
SELECT s.semester_id, s.semester_name
FROM Semesters s
LEFT JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON se.semester_id = s.semester_id
WHERE se.student_enrolment_id IS NULL
views.description: All semesters that have no student enrolment records (semesters with zero linked enrollments).

provenance.question: Which semesters do not have any student enrolled? List the semester name.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Return the names of semesters that have no students enrolled in them.
Required outputs: semester name
Filters: Include only semesters for which there exists zero enrollment records linking any student to that semester (i.e., no student is enrolled in that semester).; Do not include semesters that have one or more students enrolled.

tests.purpose: No duplicate semester_id in the view (grain is semester_id)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT semester_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM semesters_with_no_enrolments GROUP BY semester_id HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Every row in the view must correspond to a Semesters row that truly has zero linked Student_Enrolment rows
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semesters_with_no_enrolments v WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Student_Enrolment se WHERE se.semester_id = v.semester_id)

tests.purpose: All semester_id values in the view are non-NULL and exist in Semesters
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semesters_with_no_enrolments v WHERE v.semester_id IS NULL OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Semesters s WHERE s.semester_id = v.semester_id)

views.name: semesters_with_enrolment_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT s.semester_id, s.semester_name, COUNT(se.student_enrolment_id) AS enrolment_count
FROM Semesters s
LEFT JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON se.semester_id = s.semester_id
GROUP BY s.semester_id, s.semester_name
views.description: Per-semester counts of student enrolment records (zero indicates no students enrolled), preserving keys to join back to semesters.

provenance.question: What is the name of the semester with no students enrolled?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Return the name(s) of the semester(s) that have no students enrolled.
Required outputs: semester name (a string)
Filters: Include only semesters for which there are zero enrollments linking any student to that semester (i.e., no student enrollment records for that semester).; Consider all semesters present in the semesters table regardless of year or term.

views.name: transcript_course_counts_min2_per_transcript_date

  t.transcript_id AS id,
  t.transcript_date AS date,
  COUNT(tc.student_course_id) AS number_of_courses
FROM Transcripts t
JOIN Transcript_Contents tc
  ON t.transcript_id = tc.transcript_id
GROUP BY
  t.transcript_id,
  t.transcript_date
HAVING COUNT(tc.student_course_id) >= 2

params.description: Each row represents a transcript (id) on a specific transcript_date with the count of student_course rows linked to that transcript, but only includes transcripts that have at least two linked courses.
params.when_to_use: To get, per transcript and transcript_date, how many student_course entries are associated with that transcript. | As a pre-aggregated source when you need transcripts that are linked to two or more course enrollments. | When joining to other data at the transcript-level keyed by transcript_id and transcript_date.
params.when_not_to_use: When you need transcripts that have zero or one course (they are excluded by the HAVING COUNT(...) >= 2 filter). | When you need counts of distinct courses or different course-level granularity — the view counts rows in Transcript_Contents (student_course_id) and does not deduplicate duplicate student_course_id values or count distinct course identifiers. | When you need a different time window or derived date grain — the view uses transcript_date as provided (exact datetime) and groups at that exact date value, so it may split what should be a single period-level record (e.g., grouping by date_trunc(day/month) is not applied). | When you need other transcript attributes not present (only transcript_id, transcript_date, number_of_courses are available). | When a different join path or additional filters are required — the view always joins Transcripts -> Transcript_Contents and applies no extra filters besides the HAVING; it does not reflect other relationships (e.g., to students or courses) that might change the intended cohort or counts.

views.name: semester_enrolment_degree_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT se.semester_id, dp.degree_summary_name AS degree_level, COUNT(DISTINCT se.student_enrolment_id) AS enrolment_count
FROM Student_Enrolment se
JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON se.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id
GROUP BY se.semester_id, dp.degree_summary_name
views.description: Per semester counts of enrolled students broken down by degree level/type (e.g., Bachelor, Master) to identify semesters with enrollments across degree types.

provenance.question: Find the semester when both Master students and Bachelor students got enrolled in.

Required outputs: semester (the semester identifier/value)
Filters: Include only semesters where there exists at least one enrolled student whose degree level/type is 'Master' AND at least one enrolled student whose degree level/type is 'Bachelor' in the same semester.

tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT v.semester_id, v.degree_level FROM semester_enrolment_degree_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT se.semester_id, dp.degree_summary_name AS degree_level, COUNT(DISTINCT se.student_enrolment_id) AS expected_count FROM Student_Enrolment se JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON se.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id GROUP BY se.semester_id, dp.degree_summary_name) b ON v.semester_id = b.semester_id AND v.degree_level = b.degree_level WHERE (b.expected_count IS NULL AND (v.enrolment_count IS NOT NULL AND v.enrolment_count <> 0)) OR (b.expected_count IS NOT NULL AND v.enrolment_count <> b.expected_count)) AS mismatches
